summary: Generalized webapp/runner.py's strategy dispatch from a hardcoded S007-only check to a STRATEGY_WORKERS registry ({'S007': _worker_s007, 'S009': _worker_s009}), and refactored bot/s009_paper.py so S009 can run multi-account through it: extracted run_cycle_for_account(account_key, creds, state, logger, ...) from run_once()'s body (mirrors bot/s007_paper.py's function of the same name/shape), parameterized by an injectable state store instead of the single global reports/paper_s009/state.json. Added migration 003 (strategy_state table, one JSON blob per account_strategy_id) + webapp/state_store.py::DBStateStore for the DB-driven path, and utils/strategy_state.py::FileStateStore (extracted load_state/save_state) for the unchanged single-account CLI path -- run_once()/--status/--loop/scripts/s009_tick.py keep writing the same file, byte-for-byte, verified via a real --status read after the refactor. _worker_s009 hardcodes broker='off'/allow_mainnet=False deliberately -- enabling real orders through the DB-driven path is a separate future decision, not a side effect. Verified end-to-end against a throwaway copy of the real DB: `webapp.runner --worker --account-strategy-id 3` (Bybit-algo009) correctly wrote a strategy_state row and updated account_strategies.status, with zero broker orders. 55 new+existing tests pass (10 bot, 13 webapp, 32 scripts).

Stopped the S009 test suite from writing into the LIVE paper ledger. run_cycle_for_account() books each closed day via append_ledger(), which resolves LEDGER_FILE/STATE_DIR from bot/s009_paper.py module globals; only one of the eleven tests (test_run_once_uses_the_module_level_state_store) patched them, so every other test that booked a day appended fake rows straight into reports/paper_s009/ledger.csv. Three such rows (day 20001, 2024-10-05, net_ret 0.02, equity 1.02) were found in the live file on 2026-08-08, written after the bot had already booked two real days -- they corrupt the only record of live performance and are exactly what --reconcile reads. Added a module-level autouse fixture _isolate_paper_dirs(tmp_path, monkeypatch) that repoints REPO/STATE_DIR/STATE_FILE/LEDGER_FILE at a temp dir for every test, mirroring the S007 positions-log cleanup fixture (decisions-log 2026-07-21). The three fake rows were removed from the live ledger (backup kept as reports/paper_s009/ledger.csv.bak-20260808-testrows); the two genuine days (2026-08-06 +1.2445%, 2026-08-07 -0.7597%, equity 1.004753) are intact and match state.json. Verified without pytest (unavailable on this bridge VM) by replaying the fixture and the stubbed engine manually and forcing the booking path with last_day = FAKE_DAY - 1: two days booked, both rows landed in the temp ledger, and the real ledger stayed byte-identical (sha256 27dd6a32... before and after). NOT fixed, reported separately: append_ledger() still writes to one global ledger regardless of account_key, so the DB-driven multi-account path would mix every account's equity curve into one file -- the per-account state store has no ledger counterpart.

Fixed a real collision left over from the S009 multi-account refactor: append_ledger() still wrote the module-global LEDGER_FILE regardless of which `state` store was passed to run_cycle_for_account(), so even after state.json was made per-account (DBStateStore), every account's day_pnl rows would still land in the SAME shared reports/paper_s009/ledger.csv -- exactly the collision that refactor was supposed to eliminate. Found because a test run of tests/bot/test_s009_paper.py (before this fix) wrote fake rows into the real live ledger; someone/something added an _isolate_paper_dirs autouse fixture there as a stopgap, which stays. Root-caused and fixed properly: run_cycle_for_account() now takes an explicit ledger_file=None param and only calls append_ledger() when one is given; run_once()'s single-account CLI path passes its own LEDGER_FILE (unchanged behavior, regression-tested), while the DB-driven multi-account path (_worker_s009) deliberately passes none and relies solely on the already-per-account StrategyLogger day_pnl events instead. append_ledger()'s own default was changed from a bound `= LEDGER_FILE` parameter (captured once at def-time, invisible to test monkeypatching) to a None-sentinel resolved fresh on every call. Also added S009 to deployment/schedule.yml (once daily, '5 0 * * *' UTC, not every-minute like S007: run_cycle_for_account has no cheap already-up-to-date short-circuit, so frequent scheduling would hit Bybit's public API for nothing; still broker='off' hardcoded, no orders regardless of cadence). Verified end-to-end against a throwaway migrated copy of the real DB: scripts/scheduler_tick.py correctly dispatched only S009 (not S007) at a simulated 00:05 UTC Monday, wrote strategy_state, zero broker orders.
